findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby syntax, causing existing discussions to fail rendering with a template error; replace it with `<%- end %>`.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Importing feed HTML through `raw_html` bypasses sanitization and preserves scripts and event handlers, allowing malicious JavaScript to execute in the forum’s origin; sanitize HTML before storing it as cooked content.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Calling `i.content.scrub` crashes when entries contain only description, summary, or content:encoded fields, aborting remaining imports; select an available content field and handle missing content.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:65 — URL conversion incorrectly resolves protocol-relative URLs against the article’s host and leaves document-relative URLs unresolved, breaking imported links and images; resolve references against the article URL using `URI.join`.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Importing feed HTML through `raw_html` bypasses sanitization and preserves scripts and event handlers, allowing malicious JavaScript to execute in the forum’s origin; sanitize HTML before storing it as cooked content.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that TopicEmbed.import() creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] (line 22 of topic_embed.rb), and in post.rb the cook method returns raw content directly when cook_method is :raw_html (lines 131-133). The content comes from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb) or remote URLs (import_remote). While ruby-readability limits tags to 'div p code pre h1 h2 h3 b em i strong a img', the RSS feed path uses CGI.unescapeHTML on content without sanitization. The raw HTML is stored and rendered directly, potentially allowing XSS if the feed contains malicious content. This is a legitimate security concern as the content bypasses Discourse's normal post cooking/sanitization pipeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65 — URL conversion incorrectly resolves protocol-relative URLs against the article’s host and leaves document-relative URLs unresolved, breaking imported links and images; resolve references against the article URL using `URI.join`.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the `absolutize_urls` method in topic_embed.rb lines 53-72, the code only handles URLs that `start_with?('/')`. This means: 1) Protocol-relative URLs like '//example.com/image.jpg' would match `start_with?('/')` and incorrectly get the prefix prepended, resulting in 'http://host//example.com/image.jpg'. 2) Document-relative URLs like 'images/foo.jpg' (without leading slash) would not match the condition and remain unresolved. The finding correctly identifies that using `URI.join` would properly handle these edge cases. This is a real bug in URL resolution logic.
